Triggerfish: Deep leathery diamond-shaped blue-grey/gold body, eye high and well behind the small mouth, erect trigger spine ahead of a broad rowing dorsal, complete caudal fin and broad anal fin. Full head-right profile. The separate lower forward fin needs an anatomy check against the triggerfish pelvic apparatus; retain the caveat.
Parrotfish: Bright turquoise/orange large scales, blunt bulging forehead, clearly painted pale fused beak-like tooth plates and broad paddle pectoral fin. Straight right-facing profile and complete caudal tail. Left tail margin is narrower than requested; beak projection is prominent.
Pufferfish: Inflated rounded balloon body, large protruding eye, small beaked mouth, short rear dorsal/anal fins and complete small caudal tail. No pelvic fin apparent; small pectoral at side. Prominent spines and oversized eye give a strongly stylized/porcupine-like appearance; retain that identity caveat. Clear margins.
Boxfish: Yellow spotted box-shaped body, large eye, pursed lips, small fins and distinct caudal stalk/tail. Full right-facing profile and clear margins. Raised plate-junction knobs look rivet-like and overemphasize the armoured carapace; flag the manufactured-looking surface for visual review.
Lionfish: Red-brown and white zebra bands run across the body and long erect dorsal spines. Broad feathery pectoral fan has separated spotted rays; rounded spotted caudal tail is complete. All tips visible with margins. Pectoral fan naturally overlaps the flank/lower fins, so hidden ownership remains an automatic-author question.
Archerfish: Silvery deep body with bold black vertical bars, large high eye and sharply upturned small mouth. Straight head-right profile, continuous dorsal and anal fins, complete caudal stalk and broad tail. Clear margins; no water jet or prop added.
Puffin: Large flattened triangular bill has orange and blue-grey bands; white cheek patch, black cap/back and white belly are visible. Two orange legs and feet are separated, folded near wing ends above the short complete tail. Toe webbing is only weakly indicated and should be checked; clear margins.
Auk: Upright black-backed white-fronted bird with a deep dark bill crossed by pale grooves, compact folded wing and short pointed feather tail. Two complete feet and leg shafts visible, though the foot gap is narrow and webbing weakly indicated. Full head-right silhouette with clear margins.
Swan: White full body, long S-shaped neck, orange bill with black base, two separated dark feet and folded wing above a complete broad tail. Webbing is visible but partially open/weak between toes. Exposed legs read tall for a heavy waterfowl; retain proportion caveat. Full head-right silhouette with clear margins.
Cormorant: Black/bronze feathered body, long slender neck, thin hooked bill and yellow gular patch. Folded wing stays above the complete stiff wedge tail. Two separated dark feet; webbing is barely indicated and toes appear mostly separate, so retain that anatomy caveat. Full head-right silhouette with clear margins.
Bittern: Buff/brown cryptic streaked body, dark crown, long pointed level bill and compressed neck; folded wing ends above a short complete feather tail. Two separated legs and long toes visible with clear margins. Head-right full silhouette; neck is deliberately neutral rather than canonical upward freeze display.
Grebe: Crested head with chestnut cheek ruff, fine pointed bill, brown folded wing and white breast/belly. Two complete separated feet but toes appear joined by webbing rather than individually lobed; leg placement/standing stance is more duck-like than a rear-legged diving bird. Tail is a short downy rump without a distinct long feather fan. Retain anatomy/layout caveats; full head-right silhouette with clear margins.
Giant Otter: Elongated dark brown body, small rounded ears, long pale whiskers and pale throat patches. Four feet separated in stride with complete broad flattened tail. Head turns slightly toward viewer and muzzle is lifted; feet look clawed/paw-like with only weak webbing. Retain those caveats.
Quoll: Brown coat with many clear white spots across back/flanks AND along the complete long tail, pale belly, pointed muzzle and large ears. All four legs/feet separated in stride. Ears are rather pointed and tail bushy/white-tipped, producing a cat/fox-like impression; retain morphology caveat while the required spot pattern is visibly present.
Mouse: Small brown/cream rodent with large rounded pink ears, pointed whiskered snout and complete long thin sparsely haired tapering tail. Four separated feet in stride; far foreleg is shorter/exposes less of its shaft but foot is distinct. Head slightly turns toward viewer, eyes stylized large. Clear margins.
Vole: Stocky rounded brown body, blunt snout, small ears and short furred tail stump, with four visibly separated feet. Tail is much shorter than many voles and needs species-identity review; its shortness must not be interpreted as anatomical absence. Slight head turn toward viewer; clear margins.
Tree Shrew: Slender brown body, very long pointed snout, large eye, small ears and complete long bushy tail. Four legs/feet visibly separated in stride with clear margins. Ears read rather tall/pointed and muzzle/face gives some fox-like stylization; retain identity caveat.
Ground Squirrel: Grizzled brown/cream coat, small rounded ears, pale eye ring, blunt rodent snout and complete short bushy tail. Four separated legs and feet in stride, clear margins. Slight head turn toward viewer and long exposed stride differ from a low resting posture but all limb tips remain visible.
Moth: Furry brown thorax/abdomen, paired feathery antennae, brown cream-patterned roof-held wings with an eyespot, and six visible separated foot tips. Wing plates overlap each other and abdomen as expected but roots/far-side ownership are hidden. Near/far leg shafts partly overlap at their roots; all tips retained with clear margins.
Aphid: Green pear-shaped wingless body, paired obvious cornicle tubes, long segmented antennae and piercing beak beneath head. Six foot tips visible and separated, though middle/far shafts overlap/attach ambiguously below thorax. Body is heavily plated/shiny for a soft aphid; retain texture/anatomy caveat. No plant/prop and clear margins.
Dobsonfly: Long net-veined mottled wings over segmented abdomen, long threadlike antennae and paired enormous curved mandibles. Six separated foot tips, partly overlapping leg roots. Mandibles are strongly toothed/stag-beetle-like rather than slender male dobsonfly tusks; abdomen has conspicuous terminal prongs. Retain identity caveats. Full silhouette but right antenna margin narrow.
Scorpionfly: Long downward rostrum, threadlike antennae, spotted narrow folded wings, six separated foot tips and recurved male terminal abdomen. The swollen terminal structure ends in a pointed claw that reads as a scorpion stinger rather than harmless genital claspers: identity/anatomy hold, not accepted. Leg roots and paired wings overlap. Full silhouette with narrow right antenna margin.
Thrips: Slender segmented golden body and conspicuously fringed narrow wings, segmented antennae and six visible foot tips. Some wing/leg roots overlap; pointed projecting mouth cone and large clawed feet are overemphasized for thrips and need identity review. Full silhouette, narrow right antenna margin.
Orchid Bee: Metallic green/blue body, transparent veined folded wings, very long extended tongue and enlarged hind tibia visible. Only five foot tips can be distinguished in this original; the far foreleg is hidden or missing. Hold for six-leg layout/anatomy, no admission. Body is partly three-quarter rather than strict side profile; clear margins.
